newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF Trust Fund Bureau debenture holdings decrease.
newsitem.headline: MOF Trust Fund Bureau debenture holdings decrease.

text.p: The amount of debentures held by the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau has decreased since the start of the current fiscal year, MOF said in a statement on Thursday.
Holdings of bank debentures decreased by around 657 billion yen in May for a total decrease of 1.224 trillion yen since the new fiscal year began on April 1, the statement said.
The Trust Fund Bureau's assets totalled 395.932 trillion yen as of the end of May, of which 7.43 trillion yen worth were bank debentures.

On Wednesday, market sources said that MOF has told issuers of bank debentures that it will not use funds from the Fiscal Investment and Loan Programme (FILP) to buy debentures with two to five years left to maturity in the April to June period.

MOF has not yet made clear, however, whether it will continue to refrain from buying such debentures after June, the sources said, adding that the FILP has not refrained from buying one-year discount bank debentures.

An official at the Trust Fund Bureau told Reuters on Wednesday that the bureau is under no obligation to buy a set amount of bank debentures each month, adding that investment activity by the bureau tended to slow down at the beginning of the fiscal year, as fund inflows tend to dwindle due to seasonal factors.
A MOF official on Thursday declined to comment when asked why debenture holdings had decreased since the start of this fiscal year.
